claim: If settings.get throws synchronously, readDefaultRange leaves pendingDefaultRead non-null forever, so firstLoad spins on microtasks and the panel never loads, not even via the 1.5 s fallback timer.
class: sentinel cleared inside an async IIFE before the outer assignment; a sync throw makes the clear run first and the assignment overwrite it, so a wait loop on the sentinel never exits
confidence: medium; reachable only if settings.get throws synchronously. The shipped facade does not: orca.settings.get returns call(...).then(...) (plugin-panel-shell-facades.js:74) and call returns a Promise for every path (plugin-panel-shell.js:97-135). Settles: a host or test stub whose get throws synchronously. The test suite only uses async throws (tests/panel.test.mjs, "settings offline").
sweep: checked-fine: load() busy flag at src/panel/panel.js:53-69 is set and cleared in try/finally with request inside try (line 62), so a sync throw still clears busy. loadBreakdown bdBusy at src/panel/panel.js:541-574 same shape. Only pendingDefaultRead has a while loop on a sentinel. not checked: other `while (x) await x` loops in the rest of src/panel (none seen in shard).
trigger: 1. Panel opens; firstLoad calls readDefaultRange (panel.js:597). 2. host.settings.get throws synchronously (not a rejected promise). 3. The IIFE try block catches it synchronously, so line 625 (pendingDefaultRead = null) runs before the IIFE returns. 4. Line 620 then assigns the resolved promise to pendingDefaultRead, overwriting the null. 5. firstLoad reaches while (pendingDefaultRead) await pendingDefaultRead (line 601). Nothing ever resets the variable, so the loop never exits; microtasks never drain, so the 1.5 s setTimeout at line 599 never fires. Demo: node script with this exact pattern, capped at 1e6 iterations, ends with pending still set and the timer only runs after the cap.
wrong: Should: an unreadable setting falls back to 7d and the first report loads. Does: the page freezes with no report.
